# Timing belt and water pump (VG33E)

> Items marked **[Partial]** are only partly confirmed by the source and need more work. They stay in the review queue and are firmed up, corrected or removed as more sources come in.

## Summary

[Partial] Loosen tire pressure and use a custom adapter to replace the timing belt and water pump. [t2000]

Remove the entire timing cover to access internal components. [t1100]

[Partial] Remove the timing belt, then replace the water pump. [t1555]

Apply blue thread lock and ensure new water pump studs do not hit the shoulder. [t1503]

## Procedure

> **[Partial]** Needs more work: the verifier could confirm only part of this procedure (the steps marked [Partial], or whether the list is complete). Steps or precautions may be wrong or missing; read the source thread before relying on it. Later runs fill it in as more sources are found.

1. [Partial] Loosen the front tire air pressure significantly to make working under the vehicle easier.
2. [Partial] Use an adapter on the harmonic balancer bolt if the stock puller is too small.

_Procedure reported by [t2000]._

<details><summary>Alternate procedure [t1100] [Partial]</summary>

1. Remove the entire timing cover to access internal components.
2. Pull off the harmonic balancer or crank pulley.

</details>

<details><summary>Alternate procedure [t1555] [Partial]</summary>

1. [Partial] Remove the timing belt.
2. [Partial] Replace the water pump.

</details>

<details><summary>Alternate procedure [t1503] [Partial]</summary>

1. Install new bolts or studs on the water pump.

</details>

## Tools

- Air tools [t2000]
- [Partial] Harmonic balancer puller with custom adapter [t2000]
- [Partial] Thread locker [t1503]

## Parts

- Blue thread lock [t1503]
- New bolts/studs [t1503]

## Tips & gotchas

- [Partial] Work in a driveway setting. [t2000]
- Let almost all air out of front tires unless you prefer standing on a stool for the work. [t2000]
- [Partial] Replace the timing belt while working in there, as it is driven by the same system and should be swapped if a new one isn't used. [t1100]
- [Partial] Use special tools for the balancer if available, but adapt with regular toolbox items if needed. [t1100]
- Apply a dab of blue thread lock to secure fasteners. [t1503]
- Ensure the bolt does not run into the shoulder (non-threaded portion) during installation. [t1503]

## Common mistakes

- Running bolts too deep into the unthreaded shoulder [t1503]
